correctness.rationale: The validity test compares Hamming distances only for distinct aligned words but must test both off-boundary splices for every ordered pair, including equal words. A constant word produces itself as a splice; any two distinct rotations of the same nonconstant word conflict via a self-concatenation. This proves the eight-class reduction in the frozen proof. An independently written direct enumeration used all 27 literal words with no rotation restriction, through size 5 for distance 2 and size 4 for distance 3. Its histograms exactly match (1,24,174,336,132,0) and (1,24,66,12,0). Heredity rules out every larger code once the tested cap is empty. The independent code also generates all simultaneous relabelings and reversals and checks the listed representatives, obtaining two size-six and ten size-twelve orbits at distance 2, and sizes two, four, six at distance 3. Reversal preserves validity by reversing and exchanging the ordered input words, swapping the two splice offsets. In the two size-six orbits the given representatives have order-two stabilizers, generated by the pure swaps of 0 with 1 and 0 with 2, respectively; conjugacy gives the asserted Burnside fixed counts. value.rationale: This is the smallest nonbinary alphabet at the standard triple length. It gives a natural finite test of how separately enforcing ordinary boundary synchronization and aligned substitution detection changes a known capacity and its equality cases. The complete labelled counts and representatives make alternative optimal dictionaries available for comparison and distinguish genuinely inequivalent choices, which capacity alone cannot do. The contribution is modest and finite, but is not a re-computation of a known unrestricted table or a claim about correcting errors at unknown boundaries.
